issues.failure_explanation:
Corollary 3.3 asserts that $E^*(u)$ is a strongly convex quadratic functional defined on all of $L^2(I, \HHilb)$ equivalent to $\|u - u^*\|_{L^2(I, \HHilb)}$. This fails for two reasons. First, for unbounded operators $A$ (such as the many-body Coulomb potential $V$ studied in Section 3), general functions $u \in L^2(I, \HHilb)$ do not lie in the domain $D(A)$ for almost every $t$, so the integrand $A u(s)$ is undefined. Second, Section 3.3 explicitly includes a time-dependent potential $B(t)$ in the Hamiltonian $H_0 + A + B(t)$ and evolution equation (2.2). However, $B(t)$ is completely omitted from the definition of $E^*(u)$. When $B 
eq 0$, the exact solution $u^*$ gives $\sqrt{E^*(u^*)} = \|\int_0^t \eexp^{-i(t-s)H_0} B(s) u^*(s) \diff s\|_{L^2} > 0$ in general, directly contradicting the stated upper bound $\sqrt{E^*(u^*)} \leq C(1+T)\|u^* - u^*\|_{L^2} = 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict $A$ to bounded operators, include the missing term $B(s)u(s)$ alongside $Au(s)$ in the Duhamel integrand, and fix the sign in Proposition 3.4; or alternatively replace the explicit pointwise integral representation with the dual norm $\|S^* u - (i\delta_0 \otimes u_0 + f)\|_{\YY_{H_0}^\dagger}^2$.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary 3.3 is invalid as stated on $L^2(I, \HHilb)$ whenever $A$ is unbounded, and fails for any system with a non-zero time-dependent perturbation $B(t)$.
issues.title: Ill-defined and false dual L2 variational formulation in Corollary 3.3
issues.why_classification: Restricting $A$ to bounded operators excludes the paper's advertised central setting of unbounded Coulomb potentials, while defining $E^*$ via the dual norm abandons the stated explicit pointwise integral formulation on $L^2(I, \HHilb)$.

issues.failure_explanation:
The statement of Theorem 4.1 places the global supremum norm $
orm{(i\partial_t)^{k+1} v^*}_{C^0(\RR, L^2(\RR^d))}$ on the left-hand side while quantifying over $t \in \RR$ with a $t$-dependent bound on the right-hand side. Because the left-hand side is independent of $t$, evaluating at $t = 0$ implies that $(i\partial_t)^{k+1} v^*$ is globally bounded on $\RR$, which is false due to polynomial growth. The proof only establishes the pointwise bound $
orm{(i\partial_t)^{k+1} v^*(t)}_{L^2(\RR^d)} \leq C_k (1 + |t|^{k/2}) 
orm{u_0}_{H^k(\RR^d)}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair:
Replace the global norm $
orm{(i\partial_t)^{k+1} v^*}_{C^0(\RR, L^2(\RR^d))}$ on the left-hand side with the pointwise norm $
orm{(i\partial_t)^{k+1} v^*(t)}_{L^2(\RR^d)}$ at time $t$ (or bound the $C^0([-T, T], L^2(\RR^d))$ norm by $C_k(1 + T^{k/2})
orm{u_0}_{H^k}$).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 4.1 formally asserts an invalid global-in-time uniform bound for the time derivatives of $v^*$ on $\RR$.
issues.title: Mismatch between global C^0 norm and time-dependent bound in Theorem 4.1
issues.why_classification: Replacing the global $C^0(\RR, L^2)$ norm with the pointwise $L^2$ norm directly aligns the theorem with its proof and preserves the full mathematical scope of the regularity estimate without altering any downstream results.
